records.label: Four families with TRIP4 or ASCC1 mutations

variants.as_reported: homozygous and compound-heterozygous nonsense and frameshift ASCC1 mutations
homozygous and compound-heterozygous nonsense and frameshift TRIP4 mutations

records.segregation: mutations cosegregated with the disease phenotype
quotes: We used autozygosity mapping and whole-exome sequencing to search for pathogenic mutations in four families. Affected individuals presented with prenatal-onset spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), multiple congenital contractures (arthrogryposis multiplex congenita), respiratory distress, and congenital bone fractures.

We identified homozygous and compound-heterozygous nonsense and frameshift TRIP4 and ASCC1 mutations that led to a truncation or the entire absence of the respective proteins and cosegregated with the disease phenotype.

records.label: Proband (female newborn)
records.age_last: died within the first days of life
quotes: The patient presented generalized hypotonia, congenital bone fractures, lack of spontaneous movements and poor respiratory effort. She died within the first days of life.
Our patient was also found to have a homozygous frameshift variant (c.157dupG, p.Glu53Glyfs*19) in ASCC1 , thereby representing the second known case.

records.label: Male sibling

phenotypes.text: same clinical presentation as affected sister (severe neuromuscular disorder)

quotes: A male sibling was subsequently born with the same clinical presentation.

records.label: Three ASCC1 families

phenotypes.text: intense oxidative rims beneath the sarcolemma on muscle biopsy
scattered sarcomere remnants with enlarged Z-bands

variants.as_reported: recessive nonsense or frameshift mutations in ASCC1, including two novel mutations

quotes: Here, we provide a clinical, histological and genetic description of three additional ASCC1 families.
All patients presented with severe prenatal-onset muscle weakness, neonatal hypotonia and arthrogryposis, and congenital bone fractures.
Sequencing identified recessive nonsense or frameshift mutations in ASCC1, including two novel mutations.

records.label: Stillbirth case

variants.as_reported: microdeletion copy number variant (CNV) of about 64 Kb, involving four exons of ASCC1

quotes: This work describes the first case of SMABF2 in a stillbirth with documented evolution of the disease in the prenatal period.
A microdeletion copy number variant (CNV) of about 64 Kb, involving four exons of ASCC1, was firstly detected by microarray analysis, requested for arthrogryposis and hydrops.
Subsequent exome analysis disclosed a nucleotide variant of the same gene [c.1027C>T; (p. Arg343*)], resulting in the introduction of a premature termination codon.

notes.statement: Giuffrida et al. (2020) stated that this stillbirth was the first case of ASCC1 compound heterozygosity due to an exonic microdeletion and a nucleotide variant. They suggested that exonic CNVs are an underestimated cause of disease alleles.
quotes: This stillbirth represents the first case of ASCC1 compound heterozygosity, due to an exonic microdeletion and a nucleotide variant, expanding the mutational spectrum of this gene.
It also provides further evidence that exonic CNVs are an underestimated cause of disease-alleles

notes.statement: Böhm et al. (2019) found intense oxidative rims beneath the sarcolemma and scattered sarcomere remnants with enlarged Z-bands in muscle biopsies from affected infants. They suggested these findings may be a histopathologic hallmark of the disorder.
quotes: The muscle biopsies from the affected infants revealed intense oxidative rims beneath the sarcolemma and scattered remnants of sarcomeres with enlarged Z-bands, potentially representing a histopathological hallmark of the disorder.

notes.statement: Böhm et al. (2019) noted that the activating signal cointegrator-1 (ASC-1) complex is a transcriptional coactivator made of 4 subunits: ASCC1, ASCC2, ASCC3, and TRIP4. They concluded that their findings point to an important role for the ASC-1 complex in fetal muscle and bone development.
quotes: The activating signal cointegrator 1 (ASC-1) complex acts as a transcriptional coactivator for a variety of transcription factors and consists of four subunits: ASCC1, ASCC2, ASCC3 and TRIP4.
emphasises the physiological importance of the ASC-1 complex in fetal muscle and bone development

notes.statement: In a female newborn with a severe neuromuscular disorder, Oliveira et al. (2017) did whole-exome sequencing assuming a recessive model. They found no disease-causing variants in genes known to cause congenital myopathies, muscle diseases or other neuromuscular disorders. They identified a homozygous frameshift variant (c.157dupG, p.Glu53Glyfs*19) in the ASCC1 gene, making her the second reported case.
quotes: Whole-exome sequencing was performed with variant filtering assuming a recessive disease model.
Our patient was also found to have a homozygous frameshift variant (c.157dupG, p.Glu53Glyfs*19) in ASCC1 , thereby representing the second known case.

notes.statement: Oliveira et al. (2017) noted that karyotyping and screening of several neuromuscular disease genes were negative in their patient before exome sequencing.
quotes: Karyotyping and screening for several genes related with neuromuscular diseases all tested negative.

notes.statement: Oliveira et al. (2017) concluded that their finding confirmed ASCC1 involvement in a severe neuromuscular disease within the spectrum of spinal muscular atrophy or primary muscle disease. They also noted that a similar disorder is caused by variants in TRIP4, which, like ASCC1, encodes a subunit of the ASC-1 complex.
quotes: This confirms ASCC1 involvement in a severe neuromuscular disease lying within the spinal muscular atrophy or primary muscle disease spectra.

A similar disorder was described in patients with recessive variants in two genes: TRIP4 (three families) and ASCC1 (one family), both encoding subunits of the nuclear activating signal cointegrator 1 (ASC-1) complex.

notes.statement: Knierim et al. (2016) used autozygosity mapping and whole-exome sequencing in 4 families with prenatal-onset SMA, arthrogryposis multiplex congenita, respiratory distress, and congenital bone fractures and identified recessive homozygous or compound heterozygous nonsense and frameshift mutations in TRIP4 or ASCC1, subunits of the ASC-1 complex, leading to truncation or absence of the respective proteins.
quotes: We report on recessive loss-of-function mutations in two genes (TRIP4 and ASCC1) that encode subunits of the nuclear activating signal cointegrator 1 (ASC-1) complex.

We identified homozygous and compound-heterozygous nonsense and frameshift TRIP4 and ASCC1 mutations that led to a truncation or the entire absence of the respective proteins and cosegregated with the disease phenotype.

notes.statement: Knierim et al. (2016) found that morpholino knockdown of either trip4 or ascc1 in zebrafish disrupted alpha-motoneuron outgrowth and formation of myotomes and neuromuscular junctions and led to a swimming defect in larvae.
quotes: Antisense morpholino-mediated knockdown of either trip4 or ascc1 in zebrafish disrupted the highly patterned and coordinated process of α-motoneuron outgrowth and formation of myotomes and neuromuscular junctions and led to a swimming defect in the larvae.

notes.statement: Knierim et al. (2016) found that ASCC1 mutant fibroblasts downregulated genes associated with neurogenesis, neuronal migration, and pathfinding (SERPINF1, DAB1, SEMA3D, SEMA3A) and with bone development (TNFRSF11B, RASSF2, STC1). They concluded that dysfunction of a transcriptional coactivator complex can result in a syndrome affecting the neuromuscular system.
quotes: ASCC1 mutant fibroblasts downregulated genes associated with neurogenesis, neuronal migration, and pathfinding (SERPINF1, DAB1, SEMA3D, SEMA3A), as well as with bone development (TNFRSF11B, RASSF2, STC1).
Our findings indicate that the dysfunction of a transcriptional coactivator complex can result in a clinical syndrome affecting the neuromuscular system.

notes.statement: Knierim et al. (2016) found that immunoprecipitation of the ASC-1 complex consistently copurified the transcriptional cofactor CSRP1. In 17.5-day mouse embryos, Trip4 and Ascc1 had identical expression patterns, with high expression in spinal cord, brain, paraspinal ganglia, thyroid, and submandibular glands.
quotes: Immunoprecipitation of the ASC-1 complex consistently copurified cysteine and glycine rich protein 1 (CSRP1), a transcriptional cofactor
Trip4 and Ascc1 have identical expression patterns in 17.5-day-old mouse embryos with high expression levels in the spinal cord, brain, paraspinal ganglia, thyroid, and submandibular glands.
